name: Mercury
shortDescription: The swift, cratered world closest to the Sun.

facts.composition: A large iron-rich core beneath a rocky silicate mantle and crust.
features: The smallest planet in the Solar System.
Its surface preserves impact craters, scarps, and ancient volcanic plains.
Water ice exists inside permanently shadowed polar craters.
curiosities: A solar day on Mercury lasts about 176 Earth days.
Despite being closest to the Sun, it is not the hottest planet.
Mercury has only a very thin exosphere rather than a substantial atmosphere.
facts.discovery: Known since ancient times because it can be seen without a telescope.
facts.earthComparison: Mercury is about 38% of Earth's diameter and has about 38% of Earth's surface gravity.

name: Venus
shortDescription: A brilliant, cloud-wrapped world with a furnace-hot surface.

facts.composition: A rocky interior beneath a thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere and sulfuric-acid clouds.
features: The hottest planetary surface in the Solar System.
Its atmosphere creates a runaway greenhouse effect.
Most of the surface consists of volcanic plains and deformed highlands.
curiosities: Venus rotates in the opposite direction from most planets.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
It is often the brightest planet visible from Earth.
facts.discovery: Known since ancient times and historically called the morning or evening star.
facts.earthComparison: Venus is about 95% of Earth's diameter and has about 90% of Earth's surface gravity.

name: Earth
shortDescription: Our ocean world and the only known home of life.

facts.composition: An iron-nickel core, rocky mantle and crust, liquid-water oceans, and a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere.
features: About 71% of the surface is covered by water.
Active plate tectonics continually reshapes the crust.
Its atmosphere and magnetic field help protect life.
curiosities: Earth is the largest terrestrial planet.
It is the only world currently known to host life.
The Moon helps stabilize Earth's axial tilt.
facts.discovery: Earth was not discovered as a planet in the modern sense; its planetary nature became clear through centuries of astronomy.
facts.earthComparison: Earth is the reference used for comparisons throughout this catalog.

name: Mars
shortDescription: The red frontier shaped by ancient water, volcanoes, and dust.

facts.composition: A rocky planet rich in iron minerals, with a thin atmosphere mostly made of carbon dioxide.
features: Home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the Solar System.
Valles Marineris forms a canyon system thousands of kilometers long.
Evidence shows that liquid water once flowed across its surface.
curiosities: Mars has seasons, polar ice caps, dust storms, and weather.
Its two small moons are Phobos and Deimos.
Robotic missions have explored Mars more extensively than any planet beyond Earth.
facts.discovery: Known since ancient times; its reddish color associated it with war in many cultures.
facts.earthComparison: Mars is about half Earth's diameter and has roughly 38% of Earth's surface gravity.

name: Jupiter
shortDescription: The enormous storm world that rules the outer Solar System.

facts.composition: Mostly hydrogen and helium, with deep layers of liquid and metallic hydrogen and a diffuse heavy-element core.
features: The largest planet in the Solar System.
The Great Red Spot is a giant long-lived storm.
Its powerful magnetic field creates an enormous magnetosphere.
curiosities: Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet.
Its four largest moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
More than twice the mass of all other planets combined is concentrated in Jupiter.
facts.discovery: Known since ancient times; Galileo observed its four large moons in 1610.
facts.earthComparison: Jupiter is about 11 times wider and 318 times more massive than Earth.

name: Saturn
shortDescription: A pale giant encircled by the Solar System's most spectacular rings.

facts.composition: Mostly hydrogen and helium surrounding deeper liquid layers and a dense core.
features: Its rings consist of countless pieces of ice, rock, and dust.
The main rings extend hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are remarkably thin.
Titan and Enceladus are among its most scientifically important moons.
curiosities: Saturn is the least dense planet and has an average density lower than water.
As of March 2025, NASA listed 274 confirmed moons.
A hexagon-shaped jet stream surrounds Saturn's north pole.
facts.discovery: Known since ancient times; Galileo first observed its unusual appearance through a telescope in 1610.
facts.earthComparison: Saturn is about nine times wider and about 95 times more massive than Earth.

name: Uranus
shortDescription: A blue-green ice giant that rolls around the Sun on its side.

facts.composition: A hot dense fluid of water, methane, and ammonia above a rocky core, beneath a hydrogen-helium-methane atmosphere.
features: Its axis is tilted about 98 degrees, producing extreme seasons.
Methane in the atmosphere gives the planet its blue-green color.
It has 13 known faint rings.
curiosities: Each pole experiences roughly 21 years of continuous darkness during part of its orbit.
Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope.
Its magnetic field is strongly tilted and offset from the planet's center.
facts.discovery: William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781, though it had previously been mistaken for a star.
facts.earthComparison: Uranus is about four times wider and about 14.5 times more massive than Earth.

name: Neptune
shortDescription: A distant cobalt world swept by the fastest planetary winds.

facts.temperature: About −200 °C mean near the cloud tops
facts.composition: A hot dense interior rich in water, methane, and ammonia, beneath a hydrogen-helium-methane atmosphere.
features: The most distant major planet from the Sun.
Its winds can exceed 2,000 km/h.
It has faint rings and dark storm systems that appear and disappear.
curiosities: Neptune was the first planet found through mathematical prediction.
It completed its first full orbit since discovery in 2011.
Triton, its largest moon, travels in a retrograde orbit.
facts.discovery: Johann Gottfried Galle observed Neptune in 1846 near the position predicted by Urbain Le Verrier.
facts.earthComparison: Neptune is about four times wider and about 17 times more massive than Earth.
